newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Qantas wins extra Philippines service.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Qantas wins extra Philippines service.

text.p: The International Air Services Commission said on Monday it would allow an additional 228 seats a week for Qantas Airways Ltd on its Philippines route.
"This allocation will enable Qantas to operate a fifth weekly B767-300 service between Australia and the Philippines," the IASC said in a statement.

The IASC also issued a draft ruling that it would renew Qantas' Hong Kong capacity agreement, which was due to expire on June 30. The Hong Kong decision meant rival Ansett Australia had failed in its application for additional capacity to Hong Kong, it said.
"The commission could only consider the Ansett request if Qantas had failed to service the routes effectively," it said.
"The commission did not believe it had any grounds to conclude that Qantas had not serviced the routes effectively."
The latest decision meant Ansett had failed to upgrade to daily its current services to both Hong Kong and Japan.
Its application for additional capacity to Japan was rejected in January.
IASC executive director Danny Scorpecci said Ansett had also withdrawn an application for capacity to Bangkok. The airline does not currently operate services to the Thai capital.
The IASC said it would also renew Qantas' capacity on its routes to Germany and Zimbabwe.
It also issued a draft determination to renew Ansett's New Zealand route capacity.
Qantas is 25 percent owned by British Airways Plc.
Ansett is jointly owned by News Corp Ltd and Air New Zealand Ltd.
